pending_interview.category: System design (general) — scalability patterns; designing common systems like a URL shortener, rate limiter, chat system, notification system
pending_interview.question: You are asked to design a distributed rate limiter — a system that enforces a rule like "each user can make at most 1,000 API requests per minute" across a backend with hundreds of servers, where any server might handle any request from any user. Walk through your high-level design: what data store would you use, where would you enforce the limit, how would you handle the fact that requests for the same user can arrive at different servers simultaneously, and what failure modes does your design introduce? How does your design change if the requirement tightens to "no more than 1,000 requests per minute, ever, with no exceptions" vs. "approximately 1,000 requests per minute is fine"?
